transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-06-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ruiz (Aureon Head of Procurement), Devon Clarke (Aureon Legal), Samir Bose (Aureon Cloud), Priya Nair (Aureon FinOps)

Summary (auto):
Quick procurement and legal alignment for commercial clearance. Discussed MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, KMS/SSO options, pricing approval path and pilot thresholds. Agreed next steps include Redwood sending redlined contracts, SE running short benchmark, and internal Aureon stakeholder confirmations.

Topics:
- MSA redlines and liability caps
- DPA and data residency / KMS requirements
- SLA availability and rollback/fallback policy
- Pricing approval workflow and pilot terms
- Benchmarking and technical acceptance criteria

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. We're planning to move fairly quickly so we'll try to keep this tight.
[00:18] Lena Ruiz: Thanks Maya, yeah procurement's on a tight cadence this quarter, we need to get an approval packet to finance by end of month, that is the driver.
[00:28] Devon Clarke: And from legal we need to understand the DPA implications and any data transfer regimes, so, yeah, EU residency or processing outside EU could matter.
[00:37] Maya Chen: Absolutely. Owen, do you want to run the tech bits briefly while I cover the contract pathway?
[00:43] Owen Patel: Sure, quick overview — from the SE side, Redwood offers hosted, dedicated and private deploys. For Aureon the two big options are dedicated pools (reserved capacity) or private VPC deploy, depending on how strict the data residency and keying needs are.
[01:02] Samir Bose: If we go private VPC, do you support customer-managed KMS? We cannot have Redwood holding keys for PII processing.
[01:10] Owen Patel: Yes you can bring your own KMS; we integrate with AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault. On-prem HSMs are supported in the private package, though it needs a short integration window.
[01:22] Devon Clarke: When you say "support" what's the audit trail? We need robust audit logs and tamper-evidence to satisfy SOC-like controls.
[01:31] Maya Chen: We do provide per-request audit logs and the private control plane exposes them via a read-only S3 bucket or syslog. We can include an SLA for log retention in the DPA appendix, Owen can point to the docs.
[01:44] Owen Patel: Link in the deck (shared) — we also have an option to ship logs to your Splunk instance.
[01:49] Priya Nair: On pricing, high level question: what's the pilot pricing for 30k requests/month? We need a floor to present to finance.
[02:00] Maya Chen: For pilots we typically offer a discounted committed rate for the first 90 days; I can include a line item in the redline package. Roughly you'd see 20-30% off list depending on model selection and whether you choose dedicated capacity.
[02:12] Lena Ruiz: Important for procurement: we need the commercial summary to show total cost of ownership for 12 months with committed discounts and an uplift if we go multi-region.
[02:22] Maya Chen: We'll prepare a 12-month TCO sheet and include both hosted and dedicated scenarios. Owen will run a quick benchmark to validate the throughput assumptions.
[02:30] Devon Clarke: Back to clause level - liability cap: our risk committee wants to cap vendor liability at a multiple of fees, typically 12 months' fees. Is Redwood flexible here?
[02:40] Maya Chen: Standard Redwood MSA currently sets liability at the greater of direct damages up to fees paid in the prior 12 months. We can discuss exceptions for enterprise contracts but that's routed through legal. We'll include our standard and note escalation path.
[02:52] Devon Clarke: Also need clarity on indemnities around model outputs — if a model generates regulated advice, what's the allocation?
[03:01] Owen Patel: There's an operational best practice we'll send — essentially we recommend guardrails and monitoring. Contractually Redwood disclaims certain third-party content liabilities but we can flag redlines where necessary.
[03:12] Samir Bose: For technical acceptance criteria for the pilot, can we define target p95 latency at 256 tokens? We want a measurable gate before finance signs off.
[03:21] Owen Patel: Yes, p95 at 256 tokens is reasonable. On hosted it depends on model but we can target 1200ms p95 as a pilot SLO; dedicated can get tighter. We'll run a 48-hour snapshot with your sample prompts.
[03:34] Priya Nair: Ok, good. For billing we need line items by model family, per-token, and a note about quantization/latency tradeoffs that might reduce cost.
[03:44] Maya Chen: We'll include per-model unit economics and recommended quantization profiles for your workload.
[03:49] Lena Ruiz: On DPA — we need to know if customer data is used for product improvement or training. Our policy forbids any training use without explicit consent.
[03:59] Maya Chen: Redwood's hosted offering has a default no-training clause for customer data unless opt-in. We'll make that explicit in the DPA redline. For private/on-prem there is zero training by default.
[04:12] Devon Clarke: Good. Data residency scenario — can you commit to EU-only processing for the pilot?
[04:19] Owen Patel: Yes, we can pin the routing to EU-hosted endpoints for the pilot and use EU-only GPU fleets. There may be a small cost uplift for reserved capacity.
[04:29] Samir Bose: Network egress — do you charge egress separately or is it in the unit cost? We need the cost model to reflect egress for multi-region fallbacks.
[04:38] Maya Chen: Egress is usually a separate line item when we cross regions; we'll include egress estimates in the TCO.
[04:45] [05:03] -- brief silence / crosstalk as doc links are shared --
[05:15] Maya Chen: I want to call out a practical product policy — we support automated fallback to a smaller model variant if capacity is constrained. That is controlled by routing policy and can be disabled if you need strict model fidelity.
[05:30] Lena Ruiz: From procurement's perspective, fallback policies are fine as long as we define acceptable model variants and there's an SLA for fallback incidents.
[05:39] Devon Clarke: SLA carve-outs — we need to ensure force majeure and scheduled maintenance windows are reasonable. Also, breach notification timelines are critical for us (48 hours preferred).
[05:49] Maya Chen: Redwood's SLA has a 72-hour standard notification window but we can agree to 48 hours contractually for priority incidents. We'll mark that in the redline package for legal to review.
[05:59] Priya Nair: On billing cadence — do you support monthly invoices with itemized usage and a PDF-ready ledger for chargeback?
[06:08] Maya Chen: Yes, monthly invoices, line-item usage by route and model. You can request detailed token-level CSVs for FinOps.
[06:16] Owen Patel: One note — for dedicated capacity, there's typically a minimum reservation period (90 days), if you need burst we can configure a burst pool.
[06:25] Samir Bose: How fast is provisioning for dedicated pools? Our infra team needs to plan GPU allocation lead times.
[06:31] Owen Patel: Provisioning typically takes 5-7 business days once the capacity profile is agreed, less if we pre-allocate from an existing pool. Private on-prem takes longer due to network/keys — usually 3-4 weeks for full on-prem setup.
[06:45] Devon Clarke: Ok. For the DPA appendix, we need to add a list of subprocessors and a flow for adding/removing subprocessors — that is a compliance requirement.
[06:54] Maya Chen: We'll share the current subprocessors list; the DPA includes a 30-day notice for new subprocessors by default but can be adjusted.
[07:03] Lena Ruiz: Procurement approval needs the negotiated exceptions documented. Can Redwood provide a one-page exception matrix?
[07:10] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll provide an exception matrix that maps MSA clauses to requested deviation and status. That's often the quickest way to route through procurement.
[07:20] Devon Clarke: A few specific redlines we'll flag: 1) data subject rights handling timelines, 2) liability cap, 3) IP carve-outs, 4) data retention windows. We'll send those as comments in the DPA.
[07:31] Maya Chen: Great, if you can send the comments inline it's easiest. We'll respond to each comment in the redline bundle.
[07:38] Priya Nair: On pilot metrics — can we define success gates: latency p95 < 1200ms, availability > 99.5% for the pilot period, and cost per 1k tokens below X (we'll supply target)?
[07:50] Owen Patel: Yes to all; we'll instrument metrics and provide a dashboard link for the pilot.
[07:57] Samir Bose: Security review — we need SSO/SAML integration and RBAC provisioning. How mature is your IdP support?
[08:06] Owen Patel: Mature — SAML/OIDC, SCIM for user provisioning, and role mappings. We'll share an integration guide and an example SCIM payload.
[08:16] Devon Clarke: Will you commit to periodic pen-testing results or at least a summary attestation?
[08:23] Maya Chen: We can provide SOC2 Type II report and a summary of pen test outcomes. For detailed pen-test artifacts we usually do an NDA exchange; we can accommodate that.
[08:33] Lena Ruiz: Another procurement ask — we have to confirm insurance levels and cyber liability. What limits do you carry?
[08:40] Maya Chen: Redwood carries $5M cyber liability in our standard enterprise package. If you need higher we can discuss.
[08:47] Priya Nair: Noted. Price approval path question — who signs at Redwood if we get to commercial approval? We need a contact and an escalation path.
[08:56] Maya Chen: Contract execution for enterprise deals is generally handled by our legal ops team; I'll include a named contact in the redline bundle and provide escalations.
[09:04] Devon Clarke: For the DPA we also need a data breach playbook with timelines and contact points.
[09:11] Maya Chen: We'll attach the incident response playbook to the DPA appendix and confirm notification SLAs.
[09:19] [09:45] -- short pause while someone searches for a doc --
[09:58] Maya Chen: Quick operational note on rollouts — we recommend canary or phased rollout per route for the first 30 days to catch regressions. This is configurable in the Console.
[10:08] Samir Bose: That would work, we want to keep noisy routes on a limited percentage early on.
[10:14] Owen Patel: The Console supports percentage rollouts and automatic rollback on error rate thresholds.
[10:20] Lena Ruiz: Timeline recap — procurement submission by end of month. What are realistic dates for our internal steps?
[10:28] Maya Chen: Proposed: Redwood sends redlines by 2025-06-12, Aureon returns comments by 2025-06-17, finance review week of 2025-06-23, execution target 2025-06-30 pending approvals.
[10:40] Devon Clarke: That aligns with our internal windows but legal may need an extra 48 hours on top of the 17th if complex redlines appear.
[10:48] Maya Chen: Understood, we'll build in a small buffer.
[10:52] Priya Nair: If finance needs to push to July that's ok but procurement wants a clear path so we don't stall.
[10:59] Maya Chen: We'll be proactive.
[11:02] Lena Ruiz: A couple of final clarifying items: 1) Are you offering any data residency guarantees in an SLA? 2) What is the rollback policy cost if we terminate early?
[11:12] Maya Chen: 1) We can contractually guarantee EU-only processing for a pinned routing for the pilot and reflect that in the DPA. 2) Early termination fees depend on the commitment type; for a 90-day pilot there's typically no early termination fee, for reserved capacity there is a prorated unwind fee. We'll document the exact formulas in the commercial appendix.
[11:30] Devon Clarke: Ok, good. Also please include a simple flow chart of procurement steps and who does signoff on what; it helps our internal tracker.
[11:37] Maya Chen: We'll include a one-page signoff flow with names and roles.
[11:41] Owen Patel: I'll start the benchmark run after the call; Samir, can you send a sample set of prompts and expected token lengths?
[11:49] Samir Bose: Yes, sending right after. Also include any concurrency patterns, we'll simulate burst patterns.
[11:55] Maya Chen: Great. Quick note on pricing flexibility — we can do a committed pilot discount and a consumption overage model; we'll show both.
[12:04] Lena Ruiz: Final: procurement will need a single PDF packet for review. Please consolidate contracts, TCO, exception matrix, and technical acceptance into one package.
[12:14] Maya Chen: Will do.
[12:18] Devon Clarke: We'll send early DPA comments inline.
[12:21] Maya Chen: Perfect. Thanks everybody. I'll follow up with the redline bundle and TCO. Owen will run benchmarks and share spreadsheet.
[12:29] [12:40] -- meeting close --

Links shared in call: https://redwood.example.com/enterprise-dpa (DPA template), https://redwood.example.com/tco-template.csv (TCO spreadsheet), deck: https://drive.google.com/example-deck

End of transcript
